symbols.name: Delta_wit
symbols.role: displayed outcome-envelope slack for the odd-\(h\) witness

symbols.name: psi
symbols.def: For each \(x\in\{1,\ldots,J\}\), \(\psi_x(P)=\{\sum_{w=1}^{S}p_w\int_0^1a_{xw}(z)\mu_{xw}(z)\,dz\}/\{\sum_{w=1}^{S}p_w\int_0^1a_{xw}(z)\,dz\}\), and \(\psi(P)=(\psi_1(P),\ldots,\psi_J(P))^{\top}\); the argument \(P\) is suppressed when unambiguous.

symbols.name: M_D
symbols.role: noise component of the normal operator

symbols.name: H_s
symbols.role: declared Holder norm of the odd witness direction

symbols.name: A_s
symbols.def: \(A_s\) is a multiplication constant for the declared \(C^s([0,1])\) norm, so \(\|uv\|_{C^s}\le A_s\|u\|_{C^s}\|v\|_{C^s}\)

symbols.name: R_wit
symbols.role: explicit Holder-radius requirement for witness membership

symbols.name: q_A_1h
symbols.role: active-only optimizer restricted to the odd-witness span

symbols.name: q_star_1h
symbols.role: full-arm optimizer restricted to the odd-witness span

symbols.name: V_A_1h
symbols.role: active-only variance restricted to the odd-witness span

symbols.name: V_star_1h
symbols.role: full-arm variance restricted to the odd-witness span

symbols.name: V_K
symbols.def: \(V_K\) is the quasi-uniform \(B\)-spline space of degree at least \(\lceil s\rceil\), dimension \(K\), containing constants

symbols.name: q_B
symbols.role: best feasible weight in a prescribed finite family

symbols.name: V_B
symbols.role: best variance in the prescribed weighting family

symbols.name: r_B
symbols.role: certified omitted-direction residual for a prescribed finite family

symbols.name: mathfrakH_N
symbols.sig: training samples of size \(N_{\mathrm{tr}}\mapsto(\widehat p,\widehat f,\widehat a,\widehat\mu,\widehat\eta,\widehat\sigma^2,\widehat\psi)\)

symbols.name: widehat_p_v
symbols.def: \(\widehat p^{(-v)}\) is the cell-mass component of \(\widehat\nu_v\)

symbols.name: widehat_f_v
symbols.def: \(\widehat f^{(-v)}\) is the density component of \(\widehat\nu_v\)

symbols.name: widehat_a_v
symbols.def: \(\widehat a^{(-v)}\) is the propensity component of \(\widehat\nu_v\)

symbols.def: \(\Phi\) is the standard normal distribution function

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with law \(P\).

standard.name: uniform density overlap on compact support

novel.justification: The condition is a transparent compatibility restriction between the observed outcome scale and a nondegenerate noise floor; it is satisfied whenever a bounded response has positive interior support slack, including rescaled bounded clinical and educational outcomes.

This paper imposes a transparent primitive restriction that every observed treatment-cell conditional outcome distribution retains at least \(v_{\min}\) residual variance. The restriction rules out nearly deterministic conditional outcomes, is meaningful for bounded responses with genuine within-cell noise, and is indispensable for a class-uniform lower bound on \(M_D\) and hence uniform invertibility of \(C\).

assumptions.condition: \(c\in\mathbb R^J\setminus\{0\}\) is fixed and may have zero coordinates.
\(\{I_v\}_{v=1}^{F}\) partitions \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(F\) is fixed, and \(\min_v |I_v|/n\) is bounded away from zero.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal P_s\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_s=\{P\text{ on }O=(W,Z,X,Y):\text{ for each }x\in\{1,\ldots,J\},\ \psi_x(P):=\{\sum_{w=1}^{S}p_w\int_0^1a_{xw}(z)\mu_{xw}(z)\,dz\}/\{\sum_{w=1}^{S}p_w\int_0^1a_{xw}(z)\,dz\},\ \psi(P):=(\psi_1(P),\ldots,\psi_J(P))^{\top},\ \tau(P):=c^{\top}\psi(P);\ B>\sqrt{v_{\min}},\ \min_{1\le w\le S}p_w\ge p_{\min},\ f_{\min}\le f_w(z)\le f_{\max},\ a_{xw}(z)\ge a_{\min},\ |Y|\le B,\ \sigma^2_{xw}(z)\ge v_{\min},\ \max_{x,w}\|(f_w,a_{xw},\mu_{xw},\eta_{xw})\|_{C^s([0,1])}\le R_s,\ \sum_{w=1}^{S}p_wa_{xw}(z)(\mu_{xw}(z)-\psi_x(P))=0\text{ for all }x\in\{1,\ldots,J\}\text{ and }z\in[0,1],\text{ with the displayed pointwise inequalities holding for all applicable }x,w,z\}\).

definitions.name: \(\tau(P)\)
definitions.construction: For every observed-data law \(P\), define \(\psi_x(P)=\{\sum_{w=1}^{S}p_w\int_0^1a_{xw}(z)\mu_{xw}(z)\,dz\}/\{\sum_{w=1}^{S}p_w\int_0^1a_{xw}(z)\,dz\}\) for \(x\in\{1,\ldots,J\}\), set \(\psi(P)=(\psi_1(P),\ldots,\psi_J(P))^{\top}\), and define \(\tau(P)=c^{\top}\psi(P)\).

definitions.name: \(L\)
definitions.construction: For \(q\in H\), define \((Lq)_x=\int_0^1 k_x(z)q_x(z)\,dz\) for every \(x\in\{1,\ldots,J\}\).

definitions.name: \(T\)
definitions.construction: For \(q\in H\), define \((Tq)(w)=\sum_{x=1}^{J}\int_0^1 b_{xw}(z)q_x(z)\,dz\) for every \(w\in\{1,\ldots,S\}\).

definitions.name: \((q_{\mathcal A},V_{\mathcal A})\)
definitions.construction: \(q_{\mathcal A}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in H}\langle q,Cq\rangle_H\) subject to \(Lq=c\) and \(q_x=0\) for \(x\in\mathcal U\), and \(V_{\mathcal A}=\langle q_{\mathcal A},Cq_{\mathcal A}\rangle_H\).

definitions.name: three-arm odd-\(h\) witness
definitions.construction: Take only the \(S=2,J=3\) submodel: \(W\) is uniform on \(\{1,2\}\), \(Z\) is uniform on \([0,1]\) independently of \(W\), \(a_{xw}=1/3\), \(c=(1,-1,0)^{\top}\), \(h(z)=2z-1\), \(\mu_{1w}(z)=\psi_1+3\gamma\omega(w)h(z)\), \(\mu_{2w}(z)=\psi_2\), \(\mu_{3w}(z)=\psi_3+3\gamma_3\omega(w)\), and \(Y=\mu_{XW}(Z)+\varepsilon_X\), where, conditionally on \(X=x\), \(\varepsilon_x\) is independent of \(W,Z\) and equals \(\sigma_x\) or \(-\sigma_x\) with probability \(1/2\) each. The witness/class nonemptiness compatibility conditions are \(p_{\min}\le1/2\), \(f_{\min}\le1\le f_{\max}\), \(a_{\min}\le1/3\), \(B>\sqrt{v_{\min}}\), \(R_s\ge R_{\mathrm{wit}}\), \(|\psi_x|\le\Delta_{\mathrm{wit}}\) for \(x\in\{1,2,3\}\), \(0<|\gamma|\le\Delta_{\mathrm{wit}}/6\), \(0<|\gamma_3|\le\Delta_{\mathrm{wit}}/6\), and \(\sqrt{v_{\min}}\le\sigma_x\le\sqrt{v_{\min}}+\Delta_{\mathrm{wit}}\) for \(x\in\{1,2,3\}\), where \(H_s=\|2z-1\|_{C^s}\), \(M_s=\Delta_{\mathrm{wit}}+3\max\{|\gamma|H_s,|\gamma_3|\}\), and \(R_{\mathrm{wit}}=\max\{1,1/3,M_s,A_sM_s^2+(\sqrt{v_{\min}}+\Delta_{\mathrm{wit}})^2\}\).

definitions.name: \((q_{\mathcal A}^{[1,h]},q_{\star}^{[1,h]},V_{\mathcal A}^{[1,h]},V_{\star}^{[1,h]})\)
definitions.construction: In the \(S=2,J=3\) odd-\(h\) witness, let \(q_{\mathcal A}^{[1,h]}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in\operatorname{span}\{1,h\}^3:Lq=c,\ q_3=0}\langle q,Cq\rangle_H\) and \(q_{\star}^{[1,h]}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in\operatorname{span}\{1,h\}^3:Lq=c}\langle q,Cq\rangle_H\). Define \(V_{\mathcal A}^{[1,h]}=\langle q_{\mathcal A}^{[1,h]},Cq_{\mathcal A}^{[1,h]}\rangle_H\) and \(V_{\star}^{[1,h]}=\langle q_{\star}^{[1,h]},Cq_{\star}^{[1,h]}\rangle_H\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H_{N_{\mathrm{tr}}}\)
definitions.construction: Partition \([0,1]\) into \(M_{\mathrm{tr}}\asymp(N_{\mathrm{tr}}/\log N_{\mathrm{tr}})^{1/(2s+1)}\) cells. On each cell use the deterministic Lebesgue-orthonormal polynomial basis of degree at least \(\lceil s\rceil\) to form empirical projections of \(\mathbf 1(W=w,X=x)Y^r\), \(r\in\{0,1,2\}\). Sum the \(r=0\) arm projections to estimate the joint \((W,Z)\) density; obtain \(\widehat f,\widehat a,\widehat\mu,\widehat\eta\) by the corresponding joint-moment ratios; set \(\widehat\sigma^2=\widehat\eta-\widehat\mu^2\); and set \(\widehat\psi_x=\{\sum_w\widehat p_w\int_0^1\widehat a_{xw}(z)\widehat\mu_{xw}(z)\,dz\}/\{\sum_w\widehat p_w\int_0^1\widehat a_{xw}(z)\,dz\}\). Clip and renormalize on observable good-denominator events and use fixed bounded measurable fallback values otherwise. Map these fits through the formulas for \(L\) and \(C=M_D+T^{*}T\).

definitions.name: \(\widehat q_v\)
definitions.construction: For fold \(v\), construct \((\widehat L_v,\widehat C_v)\) from \(\widehat\nu_v\) and set \(\widehat q_v=\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in V_{K_n}^{J}}\langle q,\widehat C_vq\rangle_H\) subject to \(\widehat L_vq=c\), using the \(L^2\)-mass-matrix normalization.

definitions.name: \(\widehat\tau\)
definitions.construction: Writing the components of \(\widehat\nu_v\) with hats and superscript \((-v)\), define \((\widehat A_vq)(O)=\sum_x\frac{q_x(Z)}{\widehat f_W^{(-v)}(Z)}[\mathbf 1(X=x)(Y-\widehat\psi_x^{(-v)})-\widehat a_{xW}^{(-v)}(Z)(\widehat\mu_{xW}^{(-v)}(Z)-\widehat\psi_x^{(-v)})]+\sum_x\int_0^1q_x(z)\widehat a_{xW}^{(-v)}(z)(\widehat\mu_{xW}^{(-v)}(z)-\widehat\psi_x^{(-v)})\,dz\). Then \(\widehat\tau_v=c^{\top}\widehat\psi^{(-v)}+|I_v|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_v}(\widehat A_v\widehat q_v)(O_i)\) and \(\widehat\tau=\sum_{v=1}^{F}|I_v|\widehat\tau_v/n\).

definitions.name: \(\widehat V\)
definitions.construction: For \(i\in I_v\), set \(\widehat\phi_i=(\widehat A_v\widehat q_v)(O_i)\), let \(\overline{\widehat\phi}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\widehat\phi_i\), and define \(\widehat V=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\widehat\phi_i-\overline{\widehat\phi})^2\).

definitions.name: Galerkin residual and gain diagnostics
definitions.construction: For each fold \(v\), define the active-only trained optimizer \(\widehat q_{\mathcal A,v}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in V_{K_n}^{J}}\langle q,\widehat C_vq\rangle_H\) subject to \(\widehat L_vq=c\) and \(q_x=0\) for every \(x\in\mathcal U\). Write \(P_{I_v}g=|I_v|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_v}g(O_i)\). On the held-out fold define \(\overline A_{v,q}=P_{I_v}(\widehat A_vq)\) and \(\widehat C_v^{\mathrm{ho}}(q,u)=P_{I_v}[(\widehat A_vq-\overline A_{v,q})(\widehat A_vu-\overline A_{v,u})]\). For \(M>K_n\), define \(\widehat N_{v,M}=\{u\in V_M^J:\widehat L_vu=0\}\), \(\widehat r_{v,M}(u)=\widehat C_v^{\mathrm{ho}}(\widehat q_v,u)\), and \(\|\widehat r_{v,M}\|_{*,v,M}^2=\sup_{u\in\widehat N_{v,M}:\widehat C_v^{\mathrm{ho}}(u,u)>0}\widehat r_{v,M}(u)^2/\widehat C_v^{\mathrm{ho}}(u,u)\). Set \(\widehat R_M^2=\sum_{v=1}^{F}|I_v|\|\widehat r_{v,M}\|_{*,v,M}^2/n\) and \(\widehat\Delta_{\mathrm{gain}}=\sum_{v=1}^{F}|I_v|[\widehat C_v^{\mathrm{ho}}(\widehat q_{\mathcal A,v},\widehat q_{\mathcal A,v})-\widehat C_v^{\mathrm{ho}}(\widehat q_v,\widehat q_v)]/n\). On observable vanishing-denominator or bad-conditioning events, use the already declared measurable clipping and fixed bounded fallback rule. The population enriched-space certificate is generated by \(r_M(u)=\langle Cq_{K_n},u\rangle_H\) on \(N\cap V_M^J\).

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_s\), the mean-Verma equality and treatment overlap imply, for every \(x\in\{1,\ldots,J\}\) and \(z\in[0,1]\), \(\psi_x(P)=\{\sum_{w=1}^{S}p_wa_{xw}(z)\mu_{xw}(z)\}/\{\sum_{w=1}^{S}p_wa_{xw}(z)\}\). Hence the observed-law ratio-of-g-formulas functional in Definition 2 equals the \(z\)-invariant common cellwise mean and therefore its identified Napkin intervention-mean interpretation, and \(\tau(P)=c^{\top}\psi(P)\). Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_s\), the averaged-score operator satisfies \(\langle A_Pq,A_Pr\rangle_P=\langle q,Cr\rangle_H\) and \(d_0I_H\preceq C\preceq d_1I_H\) for constants \(0<d_0\le d_1<\infty\). The complete regular influence-function class for \(\tau(P)\) in the mean-scale Napkin model is \(\{A_Pq:q\in H,\ Lq=c\}\). Consequently, \(G=LC^{-1}L^{*}\) is uniformly positive definite, \(q^{\star}=C^{-1}L^{*}G^{-1}c\) is the unique efficient weight, and the semiparametric efficiency bound is \(V^{\star}=c^{\top}G^{-1}c\).
statements.justification: This is the exact global information bound needed before an attaining estimator can be assessed.
statements.gap: \cite{NabiGuoLiu2026VermaEfficiency} gives abstract single-constraint projection geometry, while the explicit full-arm averaged operator, uniform coercivity, and contrast solution are not stated there.
statements.consumer: Applied Napkin analyses with continuous school-performance or biomarker variables obtain a single benchmark variance for any education or treatment contrast.

statements.statement: For every finite prescribed linear subspace \(\mathcal B\subset H\) satisfying \(\{q\in\mathcal B:Lq=c\}\ne\varnothing\), let \(q_{\mathcal B}\) be its constrained optimizer and define its certified omitted-direction residual by \(r_{\mathcal B}(u)=\langle Cq_{\mathcal B},u\rangle_H\) for \(u\in N=\ker L\). Then \(V_{\mathcal B}-V^{\star}=\|r_{\mathcal B}\|_{(N,\|\cdot\|_C)^{*}}^2\). Hence \(V^{\star}=V_{\mathcal B}\) if and only if \(r_{\mathcal B}=0\), equivalently \(q^{\star}\in\mathcal B\), while \(V^{\star}<V_{\mathcal B}\) if and only if \(r_{\mathcal B}\ne0\). This conclusion holds separately for every member of any finite collection of feasible prescribed families.
statements.justification: The exact residual identity makes familywise strict dominance over prescribed finite weighting dictionaries testable rather than merely variational.
statements.gap: \cite{GuoLiuBenkeserNabi2026Napkin} optimizes only inside a finite affine family for continuous \(Z\); this theorem supplies the global target and the exact equality frontier.
statements.consumer: Users can determine whether enriching the published weighting dictionary can still reduce asymptotic variance.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(S\) and fixed \(J\ge3\), let \(\mathcal A=\{x:c_x\ne0\}\), \(\mathcal U=\{x:c_x=0\}\), and let \(q_{\mathcal A}\) be the active-only optimizer. Then \(q^{\star}=q_{\mathcal A}-\Pi_N^Cq_{\mathcal A}\) and \(V_{\mathcal A}-V^{\star}=\|\Pi_N^Cq_{\mathcal A}\|_C^2\). Strict gain \(V_{\mathcal A}>V^{\star}\) holds if and only if, for some \(x\in\mathcal U\), \((Cq_{\mathcal A})_x\notin\operatorname{span}\{k_x\}\). The strict-gain laws form a relatively open subset of \(\mathcal P_s\) under the primitive sup-norm topology.
statements.justification: It identifies exactly when nominally irrelevant arms become efficiency-improving control variates and shows that the phenomenon is stable under primitive perturbations.
statements.gap: Neither \cite{GuoLiuBenkeserNabi2026Napkin} nor \cite{Cattaneo2010Multivalued} characterizes zero-contrast-arm gains under a cross-arm Verma restriction.
statements.consumer: Analysts estimating a contrast between two education levels learn when observations from a third level must remain in the efficient score.

statements.statement: In the \(S=2,J=3\) odd-\(h\) construction, suppose the witness/class nonemptiness compatibility conditions \(p_{\min}\le1/2\), \(f_{\min}\le1\le f_{\max}\), \(a_{\min}\le1/3\), \(B>\sqrt{v_{\min}}\), and \(R_s\ge R_{\mathrm{wit}}\) hold, together with \(|\psi_x(P)|\le\Delta_{\mathrm{wit}}\), \(0<|\gamma|,|\gamma_3|\le\Delta_{\mathrm{wit}}/6\), and \(\sqrt{v_{\min}}\le\sigma_x\le\sqrt{v_{\min}}+\Delta_{\mathrm{wit}}\). Then \(\|f_w\|_{C^s}=1\), \(\|a_{xw}\|_{C^s}=1/3\), \(\|\mu_{xw}\|_{C^s}\le M_s\), and, because \(\eta_{xw}=\mu_{xw}^2+\sigma_x^2\), \(\|\eta_{xw}\|_{C^s}\le A_sM_s^2+(\sqrt{v_{\min}}+\Delta_{\mathrm{wit}})^2\le R_{\mathrm{wit}}\le R_s\). Every outcome support point satisfies \(|Y|\le\sqrt{v_{\min}}+(5/2)\Delta_{\mathrm{wit}}<B\), \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid X=x,W,Z)=\sigma_x^2\ge v_{\min}\), and the mean-Verma restriction holds, so the constructed law belongs to \(\mathcal P_s\). For the distinct optimizers restricted to \(\operatorname{span}\{1,h\}^3\), the exact variance gain is \(V_{\mathcal A}^{[1,h]}-V_{\star}^{[1,h]}=3\gamma^2\gamma_3^2/(\sigma_3^2/3+2\gamma_3^2)>0\). For the unrestricted active-only optimizer, symmetry gives \(q_{\mathcal A,1}(z)=3d(z)^{-1}/\int_0^1d(u)^{-1}\,du\) and \(\langle h,q_{\mathcal A,1}\rangle_{L^2}=0\), where \(d(z)=\sigma_1^2/3+2\gamma^2h(z)^2\). Its omitted inactive-arm direction is therefore \((Cq_{\mathcal A})_3(z)=-\gamma\gamma_3h(z)q_{\mathcal A,1}(z)\notin\operatorname{span}\{k_3\}\), because \(k_3=1/3\) and the displayed nonzero function is odd. The unused-arm frontier consequently yields the unrestricted strict inequality \(V_{\mathcal A}>V^{\star}\).
statements.justification: The explicit construction certifies that the general inactive-arm frontier is nonempty without conflating a three-arm example with the arbitrary-\(S,J\) theorem.
statements.gap: The adjacent Napkin and multivalued-treatment efficiency results do not exhibit a bounded smooth law with a checked positive zero-contrast-arm gain.
statements.consumer: The witness supplies a regression test for full-arm solvers and a concrete design template for simulations that isolate cross-arm efficiency gains.

statements.statement: Can the learner \(\mathfrak H_{N_{\mathrm{tr}}}\) be shown, by one finite-sample measurable construction covering endpoint and interior cells, to satisfy a uniform polynomial-tail event on which all joint moments and ratio nuisances have sup-norm error at most a constant times \(\rho_n\), every denominator and clipping or fallback branch is controlled, and the induced operators obey \(\|\widehat C_v-C\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|\widehat L_v-L\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_n)\) with no factor depending on \(K_n\)?
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing primitive theorem step; without it, the global attainment claim would assume rather than derive the learned-operator rate.
statements.gap: \cite{CattaneoChandakJanssonMa2024Boundary} controls boundary-adaptive conditional-density processes, and \cite{CattaneoFarrellFeng2020PartitionSeries} controls local series fits, but neither assembles the clipped fold-trained Napkin nuisance tuple and its operator image.
statements.consumer: The result supplies a verifiable learner class for this estimator and a reusable route for other finite-stratum generated semiparametric operators.

statements.statement: On the event in Open-ended Question 1, if \(q_{K_n}\) is the population constrained minimizer over \(V_{K_n}^J\), then uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_s\), \(\|q_{K_n}-q^{\star}\|_H=O(K_n^{-s})\), \(\|\widehat q_v-q_{K_n}\|_H=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_n)\), and \(\|\widehat q_v\|_{\infty}=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Hence \(\|\widehat q_v-q^{\star}\|_H=O_{\mathbb P}(K_n^{-s}+\rho_n)\), with no multiplicative \(K_n\) term.
statements.justification: Dimension-free saddle-point stability keeps the feasible root-\(n\) window open.
statements.gap: \cite{BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovKato2015Series} controls empirical Gram matrices, while this lemma exploits multiplication plus fixed arm rank and an \(L^2\)-normalized KKT system.
statements.consumer: The lemma allows the number of score directions to grow while preserving a stable implementable optimizer.

statements.statement: Conditionally on training fold \(T_v\), the exact bias \(R_v=c^{\top}\widehat\psi^{(-v)}+P\widehat A_v\widehat q_v-\tau\) equals \((\widehat\psi^{(-v)}-\psi)^{\top}(\widehat L_v-L)\widehat q_v+\sum_{x=1}^{J}\int_0^1\widehat q_{v,x}(z)E_W[\{f_W(z)-\widehat f_W^{(-v)}(z)\}/\widehat f_W^{(-v)}(z)\{a_{xW}(z)(\mu_{xW}(z)-\widehat\mu_{xW}^{(-v)}(z))+(a_{xW}(z)-\widehat a_{xW}^{(-v)}(z))(\widehat\mu_{xW}^{(-v)}(z)-\widehat\psi_x^{(-v)})\}]\,dz\). Therefore \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_s}\sqrt n|R_v|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).
statements.justification: The identity exposes the normalization and density errors as products even though the optimal score itself is trained.
statements.gap: \cite{NeweyRobins2018CrossFitRemainders} gives product remainders for average linear functionals, not this weighted-Verma identity with an estimated constrained inverse operator.
statements.consumer: The exact formula tells practitioners which nuisance pairs must be improved when a held-out bias diagnostic is large.

statements.statement: For the explicit primitive learner \(\mathfrak H_{N_{\mathrm{tr}}}\), including the endpoint, denominator, clipping, fallback, and measurability proof obligation in Open-ended Question 1, and under \(K_n=\lceil n^{\kappa}\rceil\) with \(1/(4s)<\kappa<1/4\), the cross-fitted estimator satisfies uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_s\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau-\tau)=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(A_Pq^{\star})(O_i)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), \(\widehat V/V^{\star}\to_{\mathbb P}1\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_s}\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|P\{\sqrt n(\widehat\tau-\tau)/\sqrt{\widehat V}\le t\}-\Phi(t)|\to0\). Thus \([\widehat\tau\pm\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\sqrt{\widehat V/n}]\) has uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\) and attains the full-arm continuous-\(Z\) efficiency bound. For every feasible finite prescribed family \(\mathcal B\), this estimator has asymptotic variance \(V^{\star}<V_{\mathcal B}\) whenever the certified omitted-direction residual \(r_{\mathcal B}\) is nonzero, with \(V^{\star}=V_{\mathcal B}\) exactly when \(r_{\mathcal B}=0\).
statements.justification: This is the headline result: primitive cross-fitted growing-sieve estimation attains the global continuous-\(Z\) bound, uniformly covers, and strictly dominates each certified deficient finite family.
statements.gap: \cite{GuoLiuBenkeserNabi2026Napkin} proves continuous-\(Z\) inference for fixed weighting choices, and \cite{ChenPouzo2015SieveWald} gives generic sieve-Wald theory; neither attains the data-dependent global Napkin score under primitive nuisance conditions.
statements.consumer: The Finnish Life Course education analysis and analogous continuous-trapdoor applications obtain efficient standard errors without choosing a small ad hoc weighting dictionary.

sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed sampling from \(P\in\mathcal P_s\) with a fixed number \(F\) of cross-fitting folds.
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes \(O_i=(W_i,Z_i,X_i,Y_i)\), with fixed finite \(W_i\), continuous \(Z_i\in[0,1]\), fixed finite treatment \(X_i\), and bounded noisy outcome \(Y_i\); the fixed envelope and variance constants satisfy \(B>\sqrt{v_{\min}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The propensity \(a_{xw}(z)\) is unknown and uniformly bounded below by \(a_{\min}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Cell masses, conditional \(Z\)-densities, and all treatment propensities have class-uniform positive lower bounds.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On each training fold, a measurable cellwise one-sided local-polynomial joint-moment learner with clipping, renormalization, and observable fallback estimates \(p,f,a,\mu,\eta,\sigma^2,\psi\); the full-arm Galerkin score is then evaluated only on held-out units.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau=\sum_{v=1}^{F}\frac{|I_v|}{n}[c^{\top}\widehat\psi^{(-v)}+|I_v|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_v}(\widehat A_v\widehat q_v)(O_i)],\quad \widehat q_v=\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in V_{K_n}^{J}:\widehat L_vq=c}\langle q,\widehat C_vq\rangle_H\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For continuous \(Z\), efficiency is approximated within a finite class generated by prespecified weighting functions.
A single Verma constraint yields an abstract Hilbert-space projection and a finite-dimensional basis approximation.
Cross-fitted regression splines yield fast second-order remainders for average linear functionals.
Orthogonal scores and cross-fitting yield root-\(n\) inference under nuisance product-rate conditions.
Boundary-adaptive local-polynomial conditional-density estimators satisfy uniform concentration and distributional approximation.
Locally supported partitioning series yield sharp approximation and uniform-inference results on compact supports.
Sharp matrix laws yield near-\(K_n/n\) conditions for least-squares series Gram matrices.
Sieve Riesz representers deliver asymptotic normality and consistent Wald variance estimation in conditional-moment models.
Multivalued-treatment efficiency is derived under ignorability without cross-arm Verma coupling.

tldr: The headline theorem gives a primitive cross-fitted growing-spline estimator for the observed-law target \(\tau(P)=c^{\top}\psi(P)\), with each \(\psi_x(P)\) defined by an explicit ratio of integrated g-formulas, that attains the full-arm continuous-Napkin efficiency bound and delivers uniform Wald coverage. The mean-Verma equality makes this functional equal to its \(z\)-invariant common cellwise Napkin intervention mean. Its asymptotic variance is strictly below that of every feasible prescribed finite weighting family whose certified omitted-direction residual is nonzero, with equality exactly at zero residual. The supporting geometry uses the coercive averaged-score operator \(C=M_D+T^{*}T\), and a separate fixed-\(S\), fixed-\(J\ge3\) theorem characterizes when zero-contrast arms strictly improve efficiency. A checked \(S=2,J=3\) odd-\(h\) law certifies nonemptiness under explicit envelope and Holder-radius compatibility conditions; its exact displayed gain concerns distinct optimizers restricted to \(\operatorname{span}\{1,h\}^3\), while unrestricted strictness follows from an explicitly nonzero omitted-direction residual. The unresolved theorem-level proof obligation is endpoint-safe finite-sample concentration for the cellwise learner at operator rate \(O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_n)\) without a \(K_n\) multiplier; failure of that rate is the kill condition.

project_justification.gap: The continuous-\(Z\) Napkin literature gives locally optimal finite weighting combinations, and the general Verma literature gives abstract projection geometry, but no primitive growing-sieve estimator is known to attain the full-arm global bound.
project_justification.niche: Fixed finite \(W\), one-dimensional smooth \(Z\), fixed \(J\), bounded outcomes with \(B>\sqrt{v_{\min}}\), overlap, and positive outcome noise make the normal operator a coercive multiplication operator plus a fixed-rank correction. This structure is narrow enough for primitive attainment and rich enough for cross-arm efficiency gains.
project_justification.fill: The headline result establishes primitive cross-fitted growing-sieve attainment and uniform Wald coverage for the explicit observed-law ratio-of-g-formulas target, with the mean-Verma restriction establishing its common cellwise causal interpretation and exact familywise strict dominance certified by omitted-direction residuals. Supporting results supply the full operator and bound, a general inactive-arm frontier, a separately verified three-arm witness whose finite-span gain and unrestricted residual arguments are kept distinct, the dimension-free perturbation and generated-score identity, and diagnostics that reveal omitted score directions.

related_work: \cite{GuoLiuBenkeserNabi2026Napkin} identifies Napkin causal means and develops robust estimators; its continuous-\(Z\) efficiency construction is restricted to finite prescribed weighting families, whereas the headline attainment theorem reaches the global optimizer and is strictly more efficient for each family with a nonzero certified omitted-direction residual. \cite{NabiGuoLiu2026VermaEfficiency} supplies the single-constraint tangent-space orthocomplement and minimum-variance projection that inform the full-arm operator theorem, but not primitive growing-basis attainment. \cite{NeweyRobins2018CrossFitRemainders} provides only the separate-sample remainder logic adapted in the exact fold-remainder lemma; the uniform positive conditional-variance floor is this paper's explicit primitive coercivity restriction, not a condition attributed to that source. \cite{ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML} supplies the cross-fitted orthogonal-score limit-theory template after the generated score is controlled. \cite{CattaneoChandakJanssonMa2024Boundary} and \cite{CattaneoFarrellFeng2020PartitionSeries} supply boundary and local-support devices for Open-ended Question 1. \cite{BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovKato2015Series} motivates mass-matrix normalization and sharp growing-series control, while the model-specific multiplication-plus-fixed-rank decomposition removes the generic sieve multiplier. \cite{ChenPouzo2015SieveWald} informs the sieve-representer variance argument. \cite{Cattaneo2010Multivalued} is the ordinary multivalued-treatment benchmark; the uncoupled reduction is included as an already-known sanity corollary and software-falsification check, not as an independent novelty result.
technical_internal_limitation: The full finite-\(n\) endpoint, denominator, clipping, fallback, and measurability concentration result in Open-ended Question 1 is an explicit theorem-level proof obligation of the headline attainment theorem, not an assumed nuisance rate. It must yield constants uniform over \(\mathcal P_s\); an unavoidable \(K_n\) multiplier that destroys the stated window is the kill condition. Numerical quadrature certification and the finite-sample allowance for the residual diagnostic are secondary proof obligations.
honest_scope: The target is the explicit observed-law ratio-of-g-formulas functional \(\tau(P)=c^{\top}\psi(P)\); under the mean-Verma equality, each \(\psi_x(P)\) equals the \(z\)-invariant common cellwise mean with its identified Napkin intervention interpretation. The proposal studies ambient mean-scale Verma efficiency at regular interior laws, uniformly attained over the fixed Holder class with the explicit compatibility slack \(B>\sqrt{v_{\min}}\). The uniform noise floor is an explicit primitive coercivity restriction of this paper: it rules out nearly deterministic conditional outcome cells and yields class-uniform invertibility of \(C\). The inactive-arm characterization and relative-openness result hold for general fixed \(S\) and fixed \(J\ge3\). The explicit odd-\(h\) nonemptiness witness is only for \(S=2,J=3\); it additionally requires \(p_{\min}\le1/2\), \(f_{\min}\le1\le f_{\max}\), \(a_{\min}\le1/3\), and \(R_s\ge R_{\mathrm{wit}}\), together with the displayed mean, coupling, and two-point-noise envelope. These are witness/class nonemptiness compatibility conditions, not assumptions driving the general strict-gain theorem. The exact closed-form gain is only for the distinct active-only and full-arm optimizers restricted to \(\operatorname{span}\{1,h\}^3\); unrestricted strict gain is certified separately by the nonzero inactive-arm residual in the general frontier. No identical witness is claimed for larger \(J\). The proposal does not claim efficiency under the stronger distributional Verma model, continuous or growing-dimensional \(W\), adaptation to unknown smoothness, weak overlap, vanishing outcome noise, or unbounded outcomes. When \(b=0\), the already-known sanity corollary recovers the ordinary block-diagonal result and supplies an unnumbered software-falsification benchmark; inactive arms provide no gain.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Section 4.3.2, Appendix S2.4.3, the proof of the continuous indexing result, and Section 7 of the current arXiv source.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Construct a primitive cross-fitted growing-spline estimator that attains the full-arm continuous mean-Verma efficiency bound with uniform Wald inference and is strictly more efficient than every feasible prescribed finite weighting family with nonzero certified omitted-direction residual; derive the target from the coercive averaged-score operator \(C=M_D+T^{*}T\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the anchor's covariance minimization over finitely many prescribed indexing densities by an infinite-dimensional constrained normal equation \(Cq=L^{*}\lambda\), then control the generated operator in \(L^{2}\)-operator norm.
seed_details.destination_search: Exact-title, exact-arXiv, and target--method searches for ``Napkin global efficiency continuous \(Z\)'', ``Napkin sieve efficiency'', and ``Verma Galerkin semiparametric efficiency'' found the two anchor preprints but no growing-sieve attainment result.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from \cite{NabiGuoLiu2026VermaEfficiency} because its Hilbert-space projection already defines the efficient influence function.
seed_details.rebuttal: That paper stops at an abstract projection and fixed finite bases; it gives neither the full-arm operator reduction, primitive inverse stability, the generated-score remainder, nor a growing-basis attaining estimator.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Section 4.3.2 and Appendix S2.4.3, where efficiency is optimized treatment level by treatment level over a finite affine family.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: For a contrast with zero coordinates, prove that inactive treatment arms lower the mean-Verma bound if and only if an unused block of \(Cq_A\) has a component orthogonal to its normalization function, with a relatively open strict-gain region and an exact three-arm odd-function witness.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace separate armwise weighting by a joint vector score and compute the \(C\)-orthogonal projection of the active-only optimizer onto \(\ker L\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining ``multivalued treatment'', ``zero contrast arm'', ``control variate'', and ``Verma efficiency'' found general multivalued-treatment efficiency but no cross-arm Verma gain criterion.
seed_details.red_team: A zero-coordinate arm is irrelevant by definition of the contrast, so any gain is a disguised covariance calculation.
seed_details.rebuttal: The Verma restriction couples arms through \(D\) and \(T^{*}T\); the proposed if-and-only-if projection condition and robust strict-gain region are absent from ordinary multivalued-treatment theory.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Introduction, Theorem 1 on probability concentration, its proof in Appendix A.4, and the conclusion.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Derive a finite-sample, fold-conditional concentration event for boundary cells, joint-moment ratios, clipping, empty-cell fallback, and measurability that implies \(\|\widehat C-C\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_n)\) without a sieve-dimension multiplier.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Change the equivalent-kernel concentration target from one conditional-density process to a finite vector of joint moments whose ratios feed a multiplication-plus-finite-rank operator.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for boundary-adaptive local-polynomial concentration combined with generated causal operators returned function and process results, not an operator assembled after fold training and clipping.
seed_details.red_team: A union bound over finitely many nuisance fits makes this an immediate corollary of \cite{CattaneoChandakJanssonMa2024Boundary}.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial step is a single measurable learner with normalization, fallback, and endpoint events whose sup-norm error maps to an operator norm independent of the growing Galerkin dimension.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Theorem 1, Theorem 2, the proof of Theorem 1, Section 5, and the concluding remarks.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Replace mean-scale one-sided weights by tensor-product test functions for the full distributional Verma restriction and prove that a regularized growing two-way Galerkin estimator attains the complete distributional efficiency bound.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Turn the closed span of residual products indexed by two functions into a coercive or explicitly regularized tensor normal operator before attempting nuisance estimation.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for ``distributional Verma tensor sieve efficiency'' and the anchor's citing record found only finite-basis projection and general conditional-moment sieve theory.
seed_details.red_team: Generic sieve minimum distance already handles infinitely many conditional moments.
seed_details.rebuttal: Generic theory does not establish completeness, coercivity, or regularization rates for the nuisance-estimated post-fixing tensor operator; these are the first changed steps.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Section 4, Remark 5, the proof of the multiple-constraint inclusion, and the concluding remarks, where reverse inclusion is left open.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: For a graph with several interacting fixing constraints, characterize the joint tangent-space orthocomplement as the closed range of a block score operator if and only if an explicit compatibility condition holds, then derive and attain the resulting bound.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct joint parametric submodels satisfying all differentiated fixing restrictions, rather than summing the normal spaces of separate constraints.
seed_details.destination_search: The nested-Markov factorization literature and the 2026 ordinary conditional-independence orthocomplement paper do not supply the reverse inclusion for interacting Verma constraints.
seed_details.red_team: The orthocomplement of an intersection is automatically the closed sum of the separate orthocomplements.
seed_details.rebuttal: That identity applies after the separate tangent spaces are shown to describe compatible submodels of the joint nonlinear model; the anchor proves only one inclusion and explicitly leaves this compatibility step open.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: Sections 2.2 and 3.3 on regular efficiency, Theorem 2, its basis-approximation proof, and the conclusion.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Let the minimum outcome-noise or overlap eigenvalue decay with \(n\), derive the frontier at which the studentized full-arm estimator remains Gaussian, and characterize the non-Gaussian or weakly regular regime beyond it.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace uniform coercivity by a triangular-array resolvent bound tracking \(\lambda_{\min}(C_n)^{-1}\) through score approximation and studentization.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for weak-overlap Verma efficiency and near-singular post-fixing score operators found weak-overlap causal inference but no Napkin-specific operator frontier.
seed_details.red_team: This is merely weak-overlap asymptotics with a renamed eigenvalue.
seed_details.rebuttal: The finite-rank Verma coupling can create weak directions not aligned with arm propensities, so the frontier must be derived from the full operator spectrum rather than a scalar propensity threshold.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: The measured-confounder extension in Appendix S3, its continuous-\(Z\) inference theorem, and Section 7.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: With an additional fixed finite measured baseline stratum, solve the conditional full-arm operators and prove that the efficient variance decomposes into between-stratum target variance plus the mean conditional bound, with an attaining estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Decompose the tangent space by the measured stratum and preserve stratum-specific causal means instead of absorbing the stratum into \(W\) with a common mean.
seed_details.destination_search: The anchor gives measured-confounder identification and local continuous-\(Z\) estimators but no conditional global operator attainment theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Finite stratification follows by repeating the no-stratum theorem in each cell.
seed_details.rebuttal: The efficient influence function requires the additional between-stratum component and a correct conditional target; nevertheless the extension is narrower than the selected kernel and is retained only as a corollary direction.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: The introduction, the continuous-\(Z\) asymptotic-linearity theorem and proof, its second-order remainder, and Section 7's discussion.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Over one-dimensional Holder classes with smoothness at or below the first-order product-rate threshold, derive the minimax rate for the identified contrast \(\tau=c^{\top}\psi\), construct a Verma-compatible higher-order estimator attaining it, and identify the exact smoothness frontier at which root-\(n\) estimation becomes possible.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct Verma-compatible least-favorable pairs for the ratio-of-integrals target and match them with a higher-order influence-function correction rather than assuming the first-order remainder is negligible.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Napkin minimax rates, higher-order influence functions under Verma constraints, and low-smoothness ratio-of-g-formulas inference found the anchor's first-order theorem and generic higher-order functional theory, but no target-specific lower bound or frontier.
seed_details.red_team: The smoothness threshold and minimax rate are immediate from generic missing-data or quadratic-functional theory.
seed_details.rebuttal: Generic lower-bound alternatives need not satisfy the mean-Verma restriction or the Napkin ratio normalization, and the matching upper bound must correct a model-specific multi-nuisance remainder.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: The introduction, Theorem 1 on the efficient influence function and bound, its three-step proof in Appendix A, and Section 7's final remarks.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: A policy-regret theorem would require covariate-indexed potential-outcome means under the Napkin restriction, while the present substrate identifies only the fixed vector \(\psi\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Identify a policy-value functional before constructing an empirical welfare score.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for Napkin policy learning and Verma-constrained optimal regimes found no identified heterogeneous policy-value target under the stated mean-scale model.
seed_details.red_team: Choosing the arm with largest estimated \(\psi_x\) is a finite-action plug-in problem, not a new policy-learning theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the stated model; without a newly identified heterogeneous value, the seed is not credible.

seed_details.anchor_location_read: The iid sampling setup, continuous-\(Z\) inference theorem, simulation design, and discussion.
seed_details.theorem_kernel: Permutation or conformal inversion would require a treatment, time, or unit symmetry group that preserves the Napkin counterfactual null.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Exhibit a valid finite-sample group action on the observed data under the null.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for conformal Napkin inference and permutation tests under Verma constraints found no symmetry implied by the observational iid model.
seed_details.red_team: Iid exchangeability alone permits permutation of units but gives no sharp randomization distribution for a causal effect.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds, so this lane is documented as obstructed rather than replaced by another M11 seed.

threads: \cite{GuoLiuBenkeserNabi2026Napkin}, Section 4.3.2 and Appendix S2.4.3, optimizes over finitely many prescribed continuous-\(Z\) indexing densities and explicitly leaves global efficiency open in Section 7.

\cite{NabiGuoLiu2026VermaEfficiency}, Theorems 1--3 and Section 5.2, supplies the single-constraint orthocomplement and abstract minimum-variance geometry but implements only finite-dimensional projections.

\cite{NeweyRobins2018CrossFitRemainders}, Sections 2 and 6, supplies the separate-sample exact product-remainder template for average linear functionals, not a nuisance-dependent inverse score operator.

\cite{CattaneoChandakJanssonMa2024Boundary}, Theorem 1 and Appendix A.4, supplies boundary-valid uniform local-polynomial concentration, not the fold-trained ratio-and-fallback learner or its operator image.

\cite{ChenPouzo2015SieveWald}, Theorem 4.1 and Section 4.2, supplies sieve-Riesz Wald theory for conditional moments but does not verify primitive Napkin nuisance learning or the global efficient score.
literature_map.settled: The causal mean is identified; the single mean-Verma orthocomplement and abstract projection principle are settled; fixed finite continuous-\(Z\) weighting families are computable.
literature_map.open: The exact full-arm operator, strict zero-contrast-arm frontier, primitive dimension-free growing-sieve stability, exact generated-score remainder, global asymptotic linearity, and uniform Wald coverage are not supplied by the adjacent threads.
literature_map.subsumption_check: No opened paper states a growing-basis estimator attaining the full continuous mean-Verma bound.

threads: \cite{NabiGuoLiu2026VermaEfficiency}, Theorem 1, characterizes the full distributional single-constraint orthocomplement by residual products and then uses finite bases.
\cite{AiChen2012SequentialMoments} develops efficient sieve minimum distance for sequential conditional moments.
\cite{ChenPouzo2015SieveWald} develops sieve Riesz and Wald inference for regular and irregular conditional-moment functionals.

literature_map.settled: The distributional orthocomplement is characterized abstractly for one constraint and finite tensor bases give local projections.
literature_map.open: No source proves coercivity or a regularization frontier for the two-way nuisance-estimated tensor operator, so attainment remains materially harder than the chosen mean-scale kernel.

literature_map.open: The reverse inclusion requires compatible joint submodels and is explicitly unresolved.
literature_map.subsumption_check: The exact open problem is confirmed, but it is a broader and less feasible paper than the finite-stratum single-constraint target.
